decision.trend: Early work on high-entropy alloys (HEAs) demonstrated that they could possess superior creep resistance at elevated temperatures (PMC5627260). Subsequent studies on refractory HEAs used nanoindentation to reveal high stress exponents and a dislocation-dominated mechanism (PMC7516662). More recent efforts explored nanolayered or multi-phase laminates for enhanced strength and crack resistance (PMC9227879), but did not fully resolve the mechanisms underlying time-dependent plastic resistance, especially for layered protective coatings. This has left open questions about the microstructural features—such as layer thickness, interface character, and stress-driven interface stability—that govern creep and plastic flow in multilayer HEA coatings.
decision.unsolved: The precise mechanism by which interfaces within HEA multilayer coatings slow or inhibit dislocation-mediated creep is still not fully understood. In particular, whether these interfaces act primarily as effective barriers to dislocation slip, as sites for dislocation locking, or as locations of localized stress accumulation remains unclear. The relative contributions of different strengthening and diffusion-blocking mechanisms have not yet been experimentally isolated under service-relevant temperature and stress conditions.
decision.lever: Perform in-situ strain-rate jump and nanoindentation creep experiments on model multilayer HEA coatings with systematically varied interface periodicity and thickness, monitoring real-time dislocation activity, interface interactions, and microstructure evolution via techniques such as high-temperature in-situ TEM or synchrotron X-ray diffraction.
decision.why: Building on existing evidence of high creep resistance in nanoprecipitate and nanolaminated HEA systems, direct in-situ observations in carefully designed multilayer coatings will allow researchers to isolate how interface architecture impedes or redirects time-dependent dislocation motion. This approach responds to the open question about the fundamental mechanism driving enhanced creep resistance in HEA multilayer coatings and will enable quantitative correlations between interface features, dislocation behavior, and long-term mechanical stability.
